filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with the Planning Department to confirm whether a formula retail Conditional Use Authorization is required or whether the restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change is permitted through zoning referral.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the prior tenant at 1701 Fillmore St was a self-service/fast food restaurant approved in 2016, the proposed use is Super Duper Burgers (a fast-casual burger chain with 11 other locations), no alcohol service is proposed, and the square footage remains approximately 2,950 square feet. Ask whether Planning Code Section 303.1 formula retail controls apply when the use does not change from restaurant to restaurant, and whether Section 178(c)(3) requires a new CUA for a change of operator of an existing restaurant. Request a written answer.

filing_playbook.action: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans for tenant improvements, including kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, ADA path of travel, and finishes, stamped by a licensed California architect, and request routing to DPH, Planning, SFPUC (FOG), and SFFD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The plans must show three-compartment sinks, a separate hand-washing sink at each work station, all food-contact surfaces sealed and smooth, the commercial hood and Type I fire suppression system sized for the cooking equipment, the grease interceptor location and size (confirm with SFPUC before submittal), accessible restrooms, and the ADA path from the entrance to all public areas. If the existing occupancy group is B (under 50 people) and the proposed load is 50 or more (A-2), clearly note the change of occupancy on the cover sheet and include an occupant load calculation. Submit the DPH plan check application in parallel, with the menu, equipment list, and scaled kitchen drawings, so plan review runs concurrently.

filing_playbook.action: Register the FOG (fats, oils, and grease) program account with SFPUC Wastewater Enterprise and submit the Installation Verification Form after the grease interceptor is installed, to qualify for the 14.2 percent sewer bill reduction.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: SFPUC assigns a Discharger Category (1–3); new restaurants must install the grease-capturing equipment before opening. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for background music, and register as an employer with the California EDD and obtain workers' compensation insurance before the first employee is hired.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket ASCAP and BMI license to play recorded music publicly; the two catalogs do not overlap, so both are needed. Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and run approximately $300–$2,500 per license. Sign up online; licenses are effective immediately. California requires workers' compensation insurance from the first employee, even part-time, and EDD employer registration within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a quarter.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline and cost are for obtaining the Conditional Use Authorization and health permit to operate, if the CUA is required. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days including pre-application meeting, formula retail neighborhood notice (Planning Code Section 311), environmental review, and Planning Commission hearing, followed by a 30-day appeal period. The base CUA fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted annually); fees rise with construction cost, and a new storefront business may qualify for a First Year Free fee waiver. The health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026–28) and building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation) run concurrently with the CUA or after it is approved. The eight comparable restaurant agency referrals on this corridor were decided in 7–40 days when no CUA was required. These figures are times to approval when the CUA and health permit are granted; they are not times to a denial or withdrawal. If Planning confirms no CUA is required for this restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change, the timeline compresses to approximately 60–120 days (building permit and health permit only), and government costs drop to approximately $2,300–$17,000 (building, health, fire, sign, and FOG permits). All figures exclude state business registration, food safety certifications, insurance, and music licenses, which are listed separately in the catalog.

records_summary: 1701 Fillmore St is zoned NCT-FILLMORE (Fillmore Street Neighborhood Commercial Transit), where restaurant use is principally permitted. The site currently operates as a self-service/fast food restaurant (approved 2016-11-15 for continuation). The address sits within two Special Use Districts—Family and Senior Housing Opportunity SUD and within 1/4 mile of an Existing Fringe Financial Service—neither of which restricts restaurant uses. The immediate area is highly active: 14 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, including 4 bars, and 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within the same radius (53 within 1,000 ft). Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 7 dated use decisions are on file: 5 approved, 1 approved with conditions, and 1 denied; too few for a meaningful approval rate.
data_gaps: Formula retail threshold analysis: the records do not show whether a 2,950 sq ft restaurant in NCT-FILLMORE triggers Planning Code §303.1 formula retail controls when the use does not change.

The pathway rules state new use permission is 'not decided' because the existing use is restaurant and the description does not say whether that business stays; no definitive zoning answer is provided for a continuation versus a new tenant.
No extracted hearing transcripts or decision rationales for the two noteworthy CUAs (Pinot's Palette, Orangetheory) or the denied entertainment CUA.

ABC concentration metrics: the records flag undue concentration but do not show the census tract ratio or whether 1701 Fillmore falls in a high-crime or over-concentrated tract (not applicable here, as no alcohol is proposed).
No details on conditions attached to the 2023 AMC Theaters CUA approval beyond the four listed.
